documents.title: Academic Honesty Guide: Honesty in Academic Work
documents.summary: The college-wide honesty policy treats AI as an outside source that must be cited and acknowledged. Uncited LLM text is a violation, instructors may set stricter assignment rules, and the document also lays out the review, outcome and appeal process.
documents.stance_why: The policy never bans AI; it names uncited use of an LLM as a violation ("Quoting or paraphrasing language from a Large Language Model (LLM) or other AI service without citing") and requires acknowledging "assistance received from ... a Large Language Model or AI service". AI is therefore allowed when acknowledged, with instructors setting extra rules, so permit.

units.why: The sentence defines the core wrong as passing off another source as one's own and explicitly names "machine-generated" sources, so it frames AI misrepresentation as an honesty violation. Coded P61 (definition of what is covered) rather than P36 because it defines scope rather than classifying a sanction route.
units.anchor: whether derived from a machine-generated source or a person
units.frag_start: Fundamentally, violation of these principles misrepresents
units.policy: Violating academic honesty principles means misrepresenting another's intellectual effort, whether derived from a machine-generated source or a person, as your own.

units.why: The list of violations includes "Quoting or paraphrasing language from a Large Language Model (LLM) or other AI service without citing", making uncited AI text an academic honesty violation. P36 fits (classified as misconduct); P24 is about the duty to disclose, whereas this sentence classifies the failure as a violation.

documents.title: Academic Honesty and AI at Grinnell (New Faculty Orientation 2025)
documents.summary: Orientation slides for new faculty. They tell instructors to decide on and clearly communicate an AI policy and explain the reasons for it. They also describe how to report suspected violations and caution against AI detectors.
documents.stance_why: The slides say Grinnell's policy "does not prohibit the use of generative AI" but "Faculty are free to develop their own course policies", and instructors "may choose to prohibit the use of AI". The college sets no stance beyond citation, so the decision goes to instructors: delegates.

notes: The CS department's own academic integrity policy (referenced by course handouts as https://www.cs.grinnell.edu/academic-integrity) returns 404, also in Wayback, so computing is marked inaccessible; recheck for a moved URL. CSC 151 syllabi from the known list are deferred. The guide overview page (node/49236) added no policy text. Art History has a departmental AI policy but is not computing. Coder B: uncovered units are the rule barring instructors from discussing suspected violations with students (two docs), the evidence standard, and the non-contract clause.
